title: Stable serialized identity
statement: Fortress-authored machine-readable entity identities MUST use a registered uppercase ASCII namespace followed by one or more non-empty uppercase alphanumeric segments separated by ASCII hyphens.
rationale: One case-sensitive, locale-independent interchange form prevents ambiguous cross-language identity, unstable normalization, and accidental duplication while allowing source languages to retain idiomatic naming.
failure_prevented: Case or separator variants that refer to the same conceptual entity, identifiers that cannot be parsed deterministically, and identity drift between tools or languages.
applicability: All stable entity and rule identities authored in Fortress machine-readable standard, project, change, command, and certification contracts.
evaluation: The Fortress core identity parser validates the registered namespace and segment grammar before an identity enters a registry or project model.

finding.message: Identity does not satisfy the Fortress stable serialized identity grammar.

remediation: Choose the registered namespace for the entity class, normalize segments to uppercase ASCII alphanumerics, separate segments with hyphens, and preserve an already published compatible identity.
exception_policy: No exemptions. External identifiers remain external data and must be carried in explicitly typed external-identity fields rather than presented as Fortress IDs.
history: Introduced during CHG-BOOTSTRAP-0001 as the first mechanically enforced draft rule.
